front_blocks.md: Define **Gibbs free energy**.

back_blocks.md: **Gibbs free energy** (*G*) is the energy that accounts for both the entropy change and the enthalpy change of a reaction, used to determine reaction feasibility.

cards.back_md: **Gibbs free energy** (*G*) is the energy that accounts for both the entropy change and the enthalpy change of a reaction, used to determine reaction feasibility.

front_blocks.md: State the Gibbs equation and give the units of each term.

cards.front_md: State the Gibbs equation and give the units of each term.
cards.back_md:
Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> = Δ*H*<sub>reaction</sub><sup>θ</sup> - *T*Δ*S*<sub>system</sub><sup>θ</sup>

Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup>: kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>

Δ*H*<sub>reaction</sub><sup>θ</sup>: kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>

*T*: K

Δ*S*<sub>system</sub><sup>θ</sup>: J K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> (must be converted to **kJ K**<sup>**-1**</sup>** mol**<sup>**-1**</sup>)

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When using the Gibbs equation, Δ*S*<sub>system</sub><sup>θ</sup> must be converted from J K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> to kJ K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> by dividing by 1000.

back_blocks.md: The units of Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup> and Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> are kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>, so Δ*S*<sub>system</sub><sup>θ</sup> must be divided by 1000 to ensure consistent units in the calculation.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The Gibbs free energy change accounts for both enthalpy and entropy changes, making it more reliable than entropy alone for determining feasibility.

back_blocks.md: Using entropy change alone is inaccurate because it ignores the enthalpy contribution. Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> combines both to give a complete picture of feasibility.

front_blocks.md: Calculate Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> for: CH<sub>3</sub>OH (l) + HBr (g) → CH<sub>3</sub>Br (g) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l) at 298 K.
Δ*H*<sub>r</sub><sup>θ</sup> = -47 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>   Δ*S*<sub>system</sub><sup>θ</sup> = -23.0 J K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>

cards.front_md:
Calculate Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> for: CH<sub>3</sub>OH (l) + HBr (g) → CH<sub>3</sub>Br (g) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l) at 298 K.

Δ*H*<sub>r</sub><sup>θ</sup> = -47 kJ mol<sup>-1</sup>   Δ*S*<sub>system</sub><sup>θ</sup> = -23.0 J K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>
cards.back_md:
Δ*S*<sub>system</sub><sup>θ</sup> = -23.0 ÷ 1000 = -0.023 kJ K<sup>-1</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>

Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> = -47 - (298 × -0.023)

Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> = **-40.1 kJ mol**<sup>**-1**</sup>

front_blocks.md: Why is it insufficient to use only entropy change to predict whether a reaction is feasible?

back_blocks.md: **Feasibility** depends on both **entropy** and **enthalpy** changes. A reaction with a negative entropy change could still be feasible if it is sufficiently exothermic. The **Gibbs equation** combines both terms to give an accurate prediction.

cards.front_md: Why is it insufficient to use only entropy change to predict whether a reaction is feasible?
cards.back_md: **Feasibility** depends on both **entropy** and **enthalpy** changes. A reaction with a negative entropy change could still be feasible if it is sufficiently exothermic. The **Gibbs equation** combines both terms to give an accurate prediction.

front_blocks.md: State the condition for a reaction to be feasible in terms of Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup>.

back_blocks.md: A reaction is feasible when Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is **negative** (less than zero). When Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is positive, the reaction is not feasible.

cards.front_md: State the condition for a reaction to be feasible in terms of Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup>.
cards.back_md: A reaction is feasible when Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is **negative** (less than zero). When Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is positive, the reaction is not feasible.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An exothermic reaction with a positive entropy change is feasible at all temperatures.

back_blocks.md: When Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup> is negative and Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> is positive, both terms in Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> = Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup> - *T*Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> are negative at any temperature, so Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is always negative.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

An exothermic reaction with a positive entropy change is feasible at all temperatures.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

When Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup> is negative and Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> is positive, both terms in Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> = Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup> - *T*Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> are negative at any temperature, so Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is always negative.

front_blocks.md: Define **feasible reaction**.

back_blocks.md: A **feasible reaction** is one in which Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is negative, indicating the reaction is thermodynamically likely to occur spontaneously.

cards.back_md: A **feasible reaction** is one in which Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is negative, indicating the reaction is thermodynamically likely to occur spontaneously.

front_blocks.md: For an endothermic reaction with a positive Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup>, at what temperatures is the reaction feasible?

back_blocks.md: At **high temperatures**. The -*T*Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> term becomes sufficiently negative to overcome the positive Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup>, making Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> **negative** and the reaction feasible.

cards.front_md: For an endothermic reaction with a positive Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup>, at what temperatures is the reaction feasible?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An endothermic reaction with a negative entropy change is never feasible.

back_blocks.md: When Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup> is positive and Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> is negative, both terms in Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> are positive at any temperature. Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is always positive, so the reaction is never feasible.

When Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup> is positive and Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> is negative, both terms in Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> are positive at any temperature. Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> is always positive, so the reaction is never feasible.

front_blocks.md: For an exothermic reaction with a negative Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup>, the reaction is feasible at **..........**  temperatures because the -*T*Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> term does not **..........**  the negative Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup>.

back_blocks.md: For an exothermic reaction with a negative Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup>, the reaction is feasible at **low** temperatures because the -*T*Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> term does not **overcome** the negative Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup>.

front_blocks.md: Explain why an exothermic reaction with a negative entropy change becomes less feasible at high temperatures.

back_blocks.md: At **high temperatures**, the -*T*Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> term becomes large and positive (since Δ*S*<sup>θ</sup> is negative). This positive term can overcome the negative Δ*H*<sup>θ</sup>, making Δ*G*<sup>θ</sup> positive and the reaction **not feasible**.
